newsitem.title: UK: EU tender result helps LIFFE grains end off lows.
newsitem.headline: EU tender result helps LIFFE grains end off lows.

text.p: LIFFE grains ended off lows as market players responded positively to the EU's tender award.
But the strength of sterling meant that they still ended with overall losses on the day.
The EU grains management committee awarded 436,500 tonnes of wheat at a refund of 10.25 Ecu. "That's got to be positive. It raised the market off the bottom," one trader said.
News of the tender award came in the final minutes of trading.
The market had been less inspired by the bids, and drifted off during the morning, the trader said.
Active May wheat closed 0.35 stg lower at 100.00 stg. At one point it had been down to 99.45 stg. May volume was 231 lots of a total 427 on wheat.
Barley volume was just 12 lots, all of it on November, which fell 0.50 stg to 92.75 stg.
A trade dinner in Manchester Thursday meant that many market players were absent, particularly during the later part of the day, limiting volume and the market's capacity to respond to the EU tender.
For that reason, traders were expected the tender to have an effect on Friday morning trading. "I'm expecting it to open up," one said.
